application_review: PROGRESS. The preceding internal-average round was rechecked before edits. The interrupted focused compilation was terminal with two rewrite errors, which were repaired in the new unregistered module. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

Projected orthogonality follows from relative orthogonality: testing a represented first projection against the intersection reduces by self-adjointness to testing the original vector against the second space. The projected representative must be pointwise unit bounded.

For unit-interval inputs from the second space, exact representatives of successive projections give a pointwise unit-bounded difference. Projected orthogonality and the original residual identity force its norm to vanish, proving preservation of the second space.

Unit-interval projection commutation is proved by membership and orthogonal-residual uniqueness. The actual intersection model retains unit-interval values and has an exactly orthogonal residual; neither result assumes commutation.

Every dual generator is pointwise unit bounded. An affine shift gives a unit-interval family still in the first space, since the constant-one image lies in both dual spaces. The verified unit-interval preservation result then proves that the second projection sends each first-space generator back into the first space.

The inverse image of the first closed space under the continuous second projection is a closed submodule. Span and closure extend preservation to arbitrary first-space vectors, without requiring all ambient Hilbert vectors to have uniformly pointwise bounded representatives.

Self-adjointness extends preservation to the orthogonal complement. Projection uniqueness proves commutation for every vector of the completed Hilbert space. The tail-containing-ultrafilter hypothesis and both positive-degree hypotheses are explicit.

Six theorems are audited. Full arbitrary-vector commutation is now proved for these actual dual spaces. Higher-order concatenation, its containment in the sum-subgroup characteristic space, the full Bessel theorem and the original main target remain unproved.
remaining: The common-system master estimates, first-order Bessel, dual energy reduction, recursion and stability are proved. Actual dual functions now have a common finite empirical approximation preserving arbitrary cell probabilities, unit bounds and uniform bounded-test correlations. Exact arbitrary-vertex reflection of the actual subgroup cube law and mixed products is now proved. Mixed cubes now have exact arbitrary-vertex duality and weighted single-vertex replacement estimates. Finite products of dual functions now have quantitative empirical approximation uniform over bounded tests. Exact translated-product expansions and extraction for each fixed test are now proved. The exact mixed face split, projected-face correlation and one-step face Cauchy-Schwarz inequality are now proved. Face energies are now identified with actual copied cube means, with nonnegativity and copy algebra verified. Arbitrary-coordinate permutation invariance, copied-mean nonnegativity and reflection bounds are now established. Full multidimensional mixed Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz, the product-root bound and the single-vertex bound are now proved. Actual dual anti-uniformity, its weighted version and the finite zero-root orthogonality characterization are now proved. Mixed dual recursion, covariance and exact subgroup-shift expansions are now established. Same-subgroup mixed-dual finite products now have an exact averaged dual representation and retain weighted anti-uniformity. The actual unit-input mixed-dual convex hull now has multiplicative and translation closure with unchanged weighted anti-uniform bounds. For varying finite groups and cell types, the exact weighted Haar Hilbert realization and vanishing-Gowers/closed-dual-span orthogonality equivalence are now proved. The dual Hilbert span now has uniformly bounded scaled-hull representatives dense in its closure; their bound may depend on the approximation. Fixed-polynomial and continuous functional calculus for scaled-hull representatives, their clipping closure, and unit-interval-valued approximation of the actual dual Hilbert projection are now proved. The actual dual projection now controls the limiting Gowers power and yields unit-interval models with arbitrarily small Gowers error along the same ultrafilter. For ultrafilters containing every tail, diagonalization now provides one exact unit-interval representative of the dual projection and residual Gowers convergence to zero. Actual unit mixed-dual-hull multiplication now preserves the closed dual space and its orthogonal complement and satisfies the genuine projection pull-out identity on represented inputs. Every unit-bounded actual representative in the closed mixed-dual subspace now multiplies that subspace and its orthogonal complement into themselves. The genuine projection pull-out identity extends to these structured multipliers without requiring cellwise convex-hull membership. Actual translations, with shifts allowed to vary by stage and cell, act linearly on weighted-Haar L2-bounded families, preserve their Hilbert distances, and have inverse-shift adjoints. They preserve the closed mixed-dual subspace and its orthogonal complement; the genuine dual projection commutes with translation on actual represented inputs. Closed Hilbert subspaces containing every selected actual unit family now contain their internal finite averages, using fixed sample counts and the original weighted L2 variance bound. Finite products of unit represented structured inputs remain structured. Taking a mixed dual along any second subgroup system preserves the first closed dual space for such inputs. A unit represented member of the first space orthogonal to the intersection has vanishing second-system Gowers seminorm and is orthogonal to the entire second dual space. For tail-containing ultrafilters and positive degrees, actual dual projections now preserve the other closed dual space and commute on the entire completed Hilbert space. The proof first transfers orthogonality using actual unit-bounded projection representatives, proves unit-interval compatibility and an exact intersection model, then extends closed-space preservation from bounded generators by projection continuity and derives full commutation by self-adjointness. Higher-order concatenation controlling dual correlations and the full qualitative Bessel theorem remain missing, as do remaining replica integration, cyclic-to-interval transfer and inverse correlator existence. Coloring-derived targets, Calibration/Alignment and final ordered positive rapidly separated monochromatic extraction remain. StrongConjecture is unchanged and unproved. No unavoidable blocker is established; publication, PR and prize application remain pending.
